subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval \u0014 parity & next steps
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@paygrid.com>, Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T16:12:00Z
Subject: PayGrid model fit eval  recap & next steps

Thanks for taking the call today  good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Key notes from the call:
- Goal: determine whether open models can meet PayGrid's quality bar vs your internal baseline ("PayGrid-Base") for intent classification + entity extraction on your payments flows.
- Acceptance threshold we discussed: parity within ~2% absolute on the primary metric (intent accuracy) and no more than 1.5% absolute drop on entity extraction F1.
- Non-functional: target P95 latency <= 120ms for single-request inference; throughput needs will be validated during the pilot.

Immediate recommendations (what Redwood can run/provide):
1) Models to evaluate (open candidates): Llama-3-70B, Falcon-180B, MPT-30B (quantized variants supported).
2) Baseline: PayGrid-Base (we will compare to the numbers you shared).
3) Deliverables: sample prompt set, eval harness (CSV of inputs/labels + scoring), and initial benchmark CSV.

Attachments included:
- paygrid-prompt-set.md (canonical prompts + edge-case examples)
- redwood-eval-harness.yml (config for runs)
- paygrid-eval-results.csv (initial pilot run summary)

Next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm scope of pilot dataset (we suggested a stratified 5k sample from transaction logs).
- Redwood: run 1-week pilot on the 3 open candidates and return detailed metrics + per-prompt failure examples.
- Schedule kickoff: propose Monday 2027-05-18 for the pilot start.

If that works Ill kick off the run and loop in our SRE/security contact for the access plan.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.ai

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@paygrid.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@paygrid.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval  recap & next steps

Thanks Lauren  this is super helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we confirm the kickoff: 

1) How are you measuring "intent accuracy" across multi-turn flows? We want to ensure the metric matches how our product routes users.
2) On latency: our spike patterns sometimes hit short bursts that require ~200 qps. Will the pilot include throughput-characterization runs or just single-request latency?
3) Regarding parity: are you measuring absolute difference or relative? Our legal team will need clear redlines if we consider replacing parts of our pipeline.

Also can you share a couple of concrete example prompts (we want to sanity-check prompt engineering effects)?

On the dataset: 5k stratified sample works  Ill confirm with Ethan on Monday and get back to you by EOD Monday 5/17.

Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Product, Payments | PayGrid
priya.shah@paygrid.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:20:00Z
Subject: Internal: quick eval summary before pilot (do not forward)

Internal notes  short summary of the initial bench runs we did against a snapshot of PayGrid sample data (attached CSV):
- Llama-3-70B (FP16)  Intent accuracy: 94.1% vs PayGrid-Base 95.0% (delta -0.9% abs). Entity extraction F1: 88.4% vs 89.5% (delta -1.1% abs).
- Falcon-180B (FP16)  Intent accuracy: 93.0% (delta -2.0% abs). Hallucination rate (free-form fields) higher on Falcon in long-context prompts.
- MPT-30B  Intent accuracy: 91.2% (delta -3.8% abs). Good throughput but lower quality on nested entities.

Quantization impact (INT8 dynamic): Llama-3 saw ~0.6% drop overall on intent metrics; Falcon ~0.9%.

Notes / risks:
- Samples where PayGrid-Base wins tend to be highly domain-specific phrasings and nested entity cases. We should prioritize those in the prompt set.
- If PayGrid requires a strict 0.5% parity tolerance, open models will need additional prompt engineering or light supervised fine-tuning.

Attachments: paygrid-eval-results.csv (per-example rows + model outputs).

Marissa
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@paygrid.com>, Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval  parity & next steps

Priya  thanks for the quick questions, answers inline below and next actions.

Q1 (multi-turn intent measurement): we score intent on the final resolved turn that triggers routing in your flow (well use the same routing labels you provided). For sequences where intermediate turns change intent we will include both per-turn and end-state metrics in the report.

Q2 (throughput characterization): yes  pilot will include both single-request latency (p50/p95/p99) and throughput sweeps to ~200 qps to reproduce your bursts. Well run both with and without batching and report cost trade-offs.

Q3 (parity math): we use absolute difference on primary metrics for parity (e.g., PayGrid-Base 95.0% vs Llama 94.1% = 0.9% absolute). For contractual redlines we can produce a short annex that defines the metric, dataset snapshot, and evaluation harness (this is common practice).

Concrete prompts: see attached paygrid-prompt-set.md  includes canonical prompts and negative examples. A quick example for intent classification: 

Prompt (canonical): 
"Customer: I see a charge for $12.99 for 'SUBSCRIPTION CHG'  I didn't authorize this.
System: Classify intent and extract merchant, amount, transaction_id if present.
"

Acceptance thresholds (final proposal):
- Primary: intent accuracy within 2.0% absolute of PayGrid-Base.
- Secondary: entity extraction F1 no more than 1.5% absolute drop.
- Hallucination: free-form hallucination rate should not exceed PayGrid-Base by more than 1.0% absolute on the annotated subset.

Pilot plan:
- Kickoff: 2027-05-18 (you to confirm).
- Dataset: PayGrid to provide stratified 5k sample + labels; Redwood to run evals on Llama-3-70B, Falcon-180B, MPT-30B (and quantized variants) and produce per-prompt failure diagnostics.
- Deliverables (end of week): full CSV with model outputs, summary deck, per-prompt failure examples, latency/throughput report, and suggested prompt/few-shot templates.

Security/access: well need a read-only S3 link or secure Drive access to the sample. Our security contact will reach out once you confirm the kickoff  theyll request the minimal data fields (no PII ideally).

If this looks good Ill schedule the kickoff and put the pilot plan into HubSpot (hubspot:HS-PG-2027-002).

Best,
Lauren
